tools.name: synap_ask
tools.description: THE recall door, for what you cannot already name (it asks the POD; to ask the PERSON, use synap_ask_person). Ask the user's Synap pod anything in natural language — it routes across all knowledge substrates (entities/notes/tasks, how-to runbooks, remembered facts/preferences, and the links/files the user kept in their Library — found by what was read from them) and returns ONE provenance-tagged answer saying which substrate answered. COST: an answer (detail full or brief, the default) runs a model and spends this key's AI budget, far smaller than its read budget; detail:'sources' runs no model and is a plain read. READ DIRECTLY WHEN YOU CAN: you have the id → synap_get_entity / synap_get_document / synap_get_session; you know the kind → synap_get_entities; you want what links to it → synap_get_graph; your open work → synap_orient. Never ask for something one of those returns. Ask when you do not know where the data is, before a non-trivial task or a question about the user's life, work, projects or preferences (the pod is their source of truth, prefer it over your assumptions), and before creating anything, to check what already exists (detail:'sources' is enough for that).

detail.description: How much answer you want. brief (default) = a few sentences, no capture suggestions — enough for lookups (who/what/where). full = the provenance-rich answer, longer; ask for it only when you need the detail. sources = no synthesis: the ranked { substrate, id, title } matches only, answer null; read one with synap_get_entity.

workspaceId.description: Optional: scope to one workspace. Omit for pod-wide recall across everything the user has. Your declared focus (synap_set_workspace_focus / synap_set_project_focus) is NOT a scope: it only ranks matching results first and hides nothing. The answer's `lens` says what was applied ({ filter, boost, source }).

projectId.description: Optional: scope recall to a project (its projects table id). Narrows results to entities linked to that project. Orthogonal to workspaceId — compose both lenses.

compare.description: A/B diagnostic: the baseline vs Horizon rankings of one pool instead of an answer. Read-only.

since.description: ISO date: only things updated from then, filtered before ranking (echoed as `window`).

tools.name: synap_get_entities
tools.description: List entities for a user filtered by profileSlug. For content/semantic recall use synap_ask. Pages: `limit` (default 50) + `offset`; a reply with `nextOffset` has more — pass it back as `offset`. Returns lean rows by default (id, title, kind, status and the kind's selected properties; `omitted` names what each row left out — pass those keys in `fields` or read one object with synap_get_entity); detail:'full' returns unprojected rows.

detail.description: lean (default) = id, title, kind, status/statusCategory/statusLabel, workspaceId, updatedAt and at most 8 of the kind's properties (select/enum, entity references and dates first; a string over 120 chars or a list over 10 items is cut, `truncated` names it with its full length); `omitted` lists the keys left out. full = unprojected rows.

fields.description: Lean only: extra property keys (or columns, e.g. createdAt) to return WHOLE on every row, never truncated — e.g. the keys a previous reply listed in `omitted`.

profileSlug.description: Profile slug filter (e.g. note, task, bookmark). Prefer this over `type`.

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID (optional)

projectId.description: Optional: narrow to a project (entity id). Orthogonal to workspaceId; usually pre-set by the connection URL.

facetSlug.description: Kind + Facets filter — only return entities carrying a live facet of this role-profile slug (e.g. 'client', 'investor'). Use synap_list_profiles to find role slugs (profileKind='role').

sortBy.description: Sort field, applied to the WHOLE set before paging (page 2 continues page 1). Default createdAt, newest first. lastInteractionAt = when we last spoke to them; never-contacted rows come last.

sortDir.description: Sort direction (default desc). e.g. 'least recently updated first' = sortBy updatedAt, sortDir asc.

lastInteractionBefore.description: ISO-8601. Only entities we last spoke to BEFORE this (exclusive). 'Not spoken to in a month' = lastInteractionBefore <now - 30 days>, includeNever true, sortBy lastInteractionAt, sortDir asc. Spoke to = a meeting, outreach sent, a dated conversation.

lastInteractionAfter.description: ISO-8601. Only entities we last spoke to on or after this (inclusive).

includeNever.description: With a lastInteraction window: also return the people never contacted (no interaction recorded). Default false.

filters.description: Filters {field, operator, value}, ANDed, max 10. field: title|type|status|createdAt|updatedAt or a property of profileSlug (bare name ok). Skill system/synap/reading.

includeFacets.description: Rows also carry their role facets.

offset.description: Rows to skip — pass the previous reply's `nextOffset` to read the next page. No `nextOffset` in a reply means it was the last page.

tools.name: synap_get_document
tools.description: Get a document by ID: its markdown `content`, the `revision` to pass back as `baseRevision` when you edit it (synap_update_document), its top-level `sections` (id, owner ai|human, title — you may only rewrite `ai` ones), and `diagnostics` (embeds that will not render, each with a `fix`; null + diagnosticsError when they could not be checked). `format: "readable"` replaces every embed with its markdown fallback. Documents are long-form content (meeting notes, research, writeups, reports); get documentId from entity.documentId or search results.

format.description: raw (default) = the stored markdown, embeds as directives (what you edit). readable = embeds replaced by their fallback text (what you quote or summarise).

tools.name: synap_get_file
tools.description: Look at a stored file (a `file` entity: an upload, an image, a PDF). Returns `url`, a signed download link that expires in 15 minutes (`expiresAt`), with `title`, `mimeType` and `size`. A PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image up to 3 MB also comes back as an image you can see (`inline.sent`); pass inline:false to get only the link. Refused when the file is outside this key's grant or the person cannot read it: the error says which (`refusedBy`).

inline.description: Default true: send a small image inline. false: the link only.

tools.name: synap_get_thread_context
tools.description: A thread's newest messages plus linked entities and documents; read it before posting. threadId: from synap_post_message or the personal channel. Or `object`: its comment threads (anchor with a pin's locator, resolvedAt); the person resolves, you reply (synap_post_message comment.replyTo).

tools.name: synap_list_proposals
tools.description: List proposals — the audit trail of AI writes. AI writes return status 'proposed' when they require human approval — this is NOT an error. Filter by status: 'pending' (needs review), 'approved', 'rejected', 'auto_approved' (the write EXECUTED immediately under governance and filed this row as its receipt — use this to show the user what you did without asking), 'reverted', 'approval_failed', 'withdrawn', 'expired' (never decided — its session closed or its window lapsed). Pass sessionId to load the **session review pack** (proposals for one focus session). userId is auto-injected from the API key if not provided.

userId.description: User ID (optional, auto-injected from API key if not provided)

sessionId.description: Focus session UUID — list only proposals attributed to this session (the review pack).

detail.description: 'summary' (default) returns one compact row per proposal — id, type, target, provenance, and a one-line summary — which is what a LIST is for. 'full' includes the entire `data` payload of every row: only ask for it when you need to inspect a specific proposal's contents, and pair it with a small `limit`.

package.description: Only proposals of this review package — the decision they ask the person: questions, access, releases, how-things-work (skills, rules, playbooks, automations, governance), data-changes, hand-offs, knowledge, bookkeeping (an agent's notes on its own session).

tools.name: synap_get_proposal
tools.description: Read ONE proposal in full — the door for "why did my write not land?". Returns the row a reviewer sees: `status`, the whole `data` payload (the operations that would apply), `summary`, provenance, and — when an approve was attempted and FAILED (`status: 'approval_failed'`) — `rejectionReason` (the classified sentence) plus `data.failure` { errorClass, providerRef, missingFields }: the fields naming what to fix. Use it after a write comes back `proposed` and the user reports a problem approving it, then REPAIR it: yours with synap_revise_proposal; another's, file the fix with `supersedes` = this id (capture, create/update_entity, run_capability). Take back yours with synap_reject_proposal (unscored). A proposal still `pending` after a failed approve attempt recorded nothing — read `data` and check the ops yourself. The raw upstream error text is deliberately NOT returned. Once applied, `landed` = the objects it made, each with `next` (what it still needs, e.g. `turn_on`).

proposalId.description: Proposal UUID, as returned verbatim by synap_list_proposals or by the `proposalId` of a `proposed` write. A leading fragment of one also resolves, but pass the full id you were given.

detail.description: 'lean' (default) = one copy of the payload (`data`), `review`, provenance, status; `request.data` and revision before/patch bodies are left out. 'full' = the whole row (about 3x larger).

tools.name: synap_template_health
tools.description: See where each workspace stands with its template — the pod's template-update radar. Per workspace: `drifted` (true = there is a step to take: a newer version, or a last update that did not finish); `state` (the last update: `active` done · `building` in progress · `awaiting-approval` its parts wait on the proposals in `awaitingApproval` · `partial`, `layer-2-not-run` or `failed` not finished); `applyWarning` (the pod's one sentence for what is left to do — relay it as is); `pendingDataChanges` (`{count, sentences, needsPodAdmin}` or null: the update changes existing data and waits for a PERSON to agree — never you; tell them what changes, in its sentences, and that they run `synap templates update <slug>` themselves, a pod owner or admin when `needsPodAdmin`); `updateProposal` (`{id}` or null: an update of this space is already proposed — point the person to that proposal, never file another); plus `installedVersion`, `latestVersion`, `warnings` and `lifecycle`: `current`, `retired` (`replacedBy` names the replacement, `retiredReason` says why; move it with `synap_retire_workspace`), `unlisted` (no longer in the catalog) or `unknown` (the catalog could not be fully read — never treat it as unlisted). The update path is `synap templates update <slug>`: run with an agent key it becomes a proposal the person approves, and data changes always need the person. Never re-apply a space that is `awaiting-approval` or has an `updateProposal`: the person's approval comes first. Read-only; scoped to the caller's own workspaces.

driftedOnly.description: When true, return only workspaces with an available update (drifted). Default false = every workspace with its health.

tools.name: synap_diagnose
tools.description: Understand what's happening / what's wrong — the pod's health door (the third door, alongside ask + capture). The MODE is derived from what you pass (never a tool name you choose): NO ARGS → whole-pod health (stuck runs, failed flows, review backlog + age, duplicate-proposal clusters, capability posture, agents hitting the daily cap) with a plain-language summary; `type` → a class as a surface (type:"proposal" = the review queue: pending count, oldest, duplicate clusters; type:"session" = stuck sessions; type:"agent" = agent roster + quality; type:"capability" = which installed verbs are turned on and which are not (a verb that is not turned on refuses to run); type:"run" = per-flow failure counts; type:"workspace" = the workspace landscape: per-workspace entity counts + which kinds live in each, PAIRWISE profile-slug overlap between workspaces, and flags for empty / duplicate-named / no-authored-identity workspaces — the "do I have too many workspaces?" read; type:"usage" = API calls per key / client / conversation / limiter class / outcome over a window (`since`, `groupBy`, `apiKeyId`, `client`; pod owner or admin only)); `id` → auto-detects what the id is (proposal / session / capability / automation-run / playbook-run / agent / entity / view / document / workspace) and explains its state + WHY; `agentId` → an agent's behavioural scorecard over its last 7 days (`window`): approve/reject/revise counts and rates, top rejection reasons, a duplicate rate read from a sample (`duplicateSample`), daily-cap posture. Backward-compatible: `runId`+`flowType` → that run's activity timeline (a capture's decision + trace events, each with a machine-readable reason + fixHint); `flowType`/`flowId` → the run feed. USER-scoped automatically.

type.description: Diagnose a whole CLASS as a surface (the review queue, stuck sessions, the agent roster, capability health, per-flow run failures, the workspace landscape, API usage).

since.description: type:"usage" only — window start, ISO 8601 (default 24 h ago).

groupBy.description: type:"usage" only — dimensions to group calls by (default client, rlClass, outcome).

apiKeyId.description: type:"usage" only — narrow to one API key.

client.description: type:"usage" only — narrow to one client (X-Synap-Client, e.g. "synap-bridge/0.6.0").

id.description: Any object id — the door auto-detects whether it is a proposal / session / capability / run / agent / entity / view / document / workspace and explains its state + why.

agentId.description: An agent-user id → its behavioural quality scorecard over its last 7 days (approve/reject/revise counts and rates, rejection reasons, a sampled duplicate rate, daily-cap posture).

workspaceId.description: Narrow whole-pod health or a class surface to ONE workspace lens (default: all workspaces you can see).

stuckThresholdHours.description: Override the 'stuck run' age boundary for whole-pod health (default 24h).

flowType.description: Back-compat run-feed grammar: restrict to one ledger. REQUIRED when runId is given (the id space differs per flow).

flowId.description: Back-compat: restrict the feed to one flow's runs (automationId / playbookId).

runId.description: Back-compat: a specific run id (or a capture's correlationId) → that run's activity timeline instead of the feed.

tools.name: synap_get_entity
tools.description: Get a single entity by ID with full details: all properties and metadata. Use after synap_ask to get complete data on a result. The id comes from synap_ask results or synap_create_entity responses.

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID (optional)

detail.description: 'lean' (default) omits `effectivePropertiesByWorkspace` — the kind's property schema re-resolved once per accessible workspace, which is 83-93% of an entity read and long enough on its own to truncate the response. You still get the entity, its profile, its own workspace's `effectiveProperties` (the schema a write to this entity is validated against), facets, externalLinks and graph, plus a `propertyOverlays` signpost naming which workspaces differ. 'full' adds the per-workspace map back — ask for it only when you need to compare lenses.

tools.name: synap_list_profiles
tools.description: List all available entity types (profiles) AND the relation types you may link them with. ALWAYS call at session start before creating entities or relations. Workspaces differ: never assume a type or relation slug exists. Returns { profiles, relationTypes }: a lightweight digest per profile (id, slug, displayName, profileKind, entityScope, applicableKinds on roles, description ≤120 chars, workspaceId), and relationTypes as slugs grouped by lens ([{workspaceId:null, slugs}] = valid everywhere, plus per-workspace groups listing only the slugs that workspace adds). detail:'full' returns complete profile rows and full relation-type rows (displayName, description, isDirectional, inverseLabel). A relation `type` on synap_capture / synap_link_entities must be one of those slugs; any other slug is rejected with the valid list. If the relation read failed you get `relationTypesError` instead of `relationTypes`. Without a workspaceId, profiles are merged across your workspaces; a workspace whose profiles could not be read is named in `workspacesFailed`, never silently dropped. A kind's fields, enums and required keys: call synap_get_entity on any existing entity of that kind (its `effectiveProperties`); over HTTP, GET /api/hub/discover?profileSlugs=<slug>. For a kind with no entities yet, a write that breaks the schema is rejected with the valid fields quoted — fix and resend once.

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID (optional — omit to list across all workspaces)

detail.description: Pass 'full' to receive complete profile rows (including renderer and uiHints columns) and full relation-type rows (displayName, description, isDirectional, inverseLabel). Omit for the lean digest (default): profile digests plus relation-type slugs grouped by lens.

tools.name: synap_get_relations
tools.description: Get all relations for an entity — inbound and outbound. Returns typed edges with sourceEntityId, targetEntityId, and relation type. Dependencies ('blocks' / 'depends_on') are included: they are stored as one dependency link, so their row carries storedAs:'link' and a link id. Check before synap_link_entities to avoid duplicates. Use to understand an entity's connections.

entityId.description: Entity UUID to get relations for

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID (optional)

limit.description: Max relations returned, newest first (default 50, max 100).

tools.name: synap_resolve_identity
tools.description: Read-only identity PRE-CHECK — call BEFORE creating an entity to decide create-vs-enrich-vs-attach_facet. Pass the strong signals you have (email/phone/url/twitter/github/externalId) and/or a title + kindSlug. Returns match:'strong' (a globally-unique signal already resolves to an entity → do NOT create; enrich it or synap_attach_facet a new role onto entityId instead), match:'weak' (same-name candidates — advisory, inspect `candidates` before deciding), or match:'none' (safe to create). This is the dedup door: an entity exists ONCE (a person, a company); roles are facets, never second entities. Never writes.

kindSlug.description: The kind (profile slug) you intend to create, e.g. person, company. A same-name match must be this kind to count as a 'weak' match; cross-kind rows still appear in `candidates`.

title.description: The name/title to check. Omit to do a strong-signal-only lookup.

signals.description: Strong identity atoms you already know. Any one match auto-resolves. Also accepted: an atom name (linkedin_url, website, twitter_handle, github_username, telegram_phone, external_id) or the property slug that carries it (linkedinUrl, twitterHandle, githubUsername, telegramPhone); any other key is refused.

properties.description: Draft property bag — strong signals are also extracted from it (merged with `signals`).

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID (optional).

tools.name: synap_get_graph
tools.description: Fetch ANY object PLUS everything it's linked to, typed. Returns { object, neighbors[], counts }. Each neighbor is { kind, subtype, name, id, edgeType, direction, via } — so you see a person linked to a deal, a skill linked to its tools, a session to its produced entities, etc. Graph by default: call this to understand an object's place in the pod before acting. Works for entity, project, view, channel, session, playbook, tool, skill, automation, document, track (a project's method: its project, sessions and playbook), proposal (what it governed and the session it was filed in) and run (an automation run: its automation and subject).

id.description: The object's FULL uuid — short ids are not resolved by this tool. Provide id OR name.

name.description: Fetch by NAME instead of id (a handle). Ambiguous names return candidates to pick from. Provide id OR name.

type.description: Object kind: entity (default), project, view, channel, session, playbook, tool, skill, automation, document, track, proposal, run.

subtype.description: Narrow a name lookup (entity profileSlug, view type, tool/skill kind). Optional.

tools.name: synap_create_entity
tools.description: Create a SINGLE typed entity — no relations parameter exists here. Use when you already know the exact profileSlug + fields: the structured, deterministic sibling of synap_capture (which parses free text). Discover slugs with synap_list_profiles; synap_ask first to avoid duplicates. A same-kind record, or one of your own pending proposals, with the same name or identity does not block: the create is filed as a proposal and the person decides (keep both, use the existing one, fill its empty fields), so reuse the existing id when it is the same thing, and say in `reasoning` why a twin is separate. Placeholder person/company titles (e.g. 'Not publicly disclosed', 'unknown') are rejected. To create an entity TOGETHER WITH its edge to another entity in one reviewable unit, use synap_capture instead, passing both `entities` and `relations` — synap_link_entities cannot target an entity this call just proposed (its id isn't live until approved). A `decision` with `decisionStatus:'proposed'` ASKS the person automatically: pass `decisionOptions` (≤8 of {label, value?, description?}) + `recommendedOption`, and `sourceSessionId` to keep the question in your session; their answer updates it. Never create a decision for an answered confirm/choose — the pod already filed it (`slot.decisionId`).

profileSlug.description: Entity profile slug (e.g., note, task, event, person, contact, company, deal, bookmark, article). Use synap_list_profiles to discover available types. The cross-cutting container that spans workspaces is NOT an entity kind — it has its own door, synap_create_project.

content.description: Markdown body (the write-up itself, not a summary). A long-form body (600+ characters, or 2+ headings, a code fence, 3+ list items or 4+ paragraphs) becomes a versioned document linked to the entity, so an entity and its body land in ONE call; a shorter one is stored inline as the `content` property. Use `description` for a short preview; do NOT stuff long text into `properties`.

projectId.description: Optional project id to file the created entity into — stamps belongs_to_project membership.

workspaceId.description: Optional: the space this entity is for (defaults to the connection's). A pod-wide kind (note, person, decision…) stays pod-wide and is filed for that space, so it shows there for its members: no synap_move_entities afterwards. A space you are not a member of is ignored. The reply's `placement` says what happened.

sessionId.description: OPTIONAL focus-session override. Leave it out and the write is attributed automatically — you do NOT normally pass this. Send it ONLY to disambiguate: when two or more of your focus sessions are open, automatic attribution deliberately declines rather than guess, and this is the only way to say which session the write belongs to. Also the way to JOIN a session another conversation started — automatic attribution never shares one across conversations. A session that isn't yours is ignored, not an error.

facets.description: Kind + Facets: attach one or more role-profiles to the new entity in the SAME call (e.g. a person who is a client + investor). A role is a facet, NOT a separate entity — resolve identity first, then attach roles here. Each item: { slug, properties? }. Only applied when the entity is created (not when the create is proposal-gated).

expectedLabel.description: The declared output slot this fulfils: its key or its label. One that names no output of the session is said in the reply's `warnings`.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional: a stable key per entity (e.g. the source file's path) so a retry after a timeout returns the entity the first call created instead of a second one.

reasoning.description: Why you are making this write, in the person's words — shown to the human who reviews it. One line.

tools.name: synap_update_entity
tools.description: Update an entity's title, description, properties (JSONB), or long-form BODY (`content`). Requires entityId from search or synap_get_entity. May return 'proposed' if the write requires review. Use for property updates and status changes. To move a status (a kind's declared lifecycle), set the property to the new option AND pass `expectedStatus` = the status you read: `conflict` means someone moved it (re-read), a move into a done/lost or human-only option proposes (the person approves it). `content` REPLACES the whole body of the entity's linked document (an alias of synap_update_document with one replace_all op): it always goes to review, and it is refused if it changes a person's section or drops an embed. To change one section or one passage, use synap_update_document instead. If the entity has no body document yet the call is refused — create and attach one with synap_create_document({ entityId, title, content }). `documentId` attaches an EXISTING document from the entity's own space as the body (e.g. one left orphaned) and always goes to review (a document from another space is refused: the person attaches it); replacing a body the entity already has also needs `replaceBody: true`; undo puts the previous body back. `profileSlug` converts it to another kind, keeping its id and links (always reviewed). `homeWorkspaceId` files a POD-WIDE record for a space so its members (and that space's apps) read it; null clears it.

profileSlug.description: CONVERT the entity to another kind (e.g. a misfiled knowledge entry → decision, issue or note). It keeps its id, links, document and history; always a proposal. Send the new kind's required properties in `properties` in the same call. An unknown kind is refused — list kinds with synap_list_profiles.

properties.description: Partial properties to merge into entity.properties JSONB

content.description: Full REPLACEMENT body (markdown) for the entity's linked document — not a patch (for a patch: synap_update_document). Read the current body with synap_get_document first. Its outcome comes back under `body` and is always 'proposed'.

expectedStatus.description: When you change the status: the status you SAW (compare-and-set). If it moved meanwhile you get { status: 'conflict', conflict: { currentStatus } } and nothing is written — re-read and decide again; never retry blindly.

hold.description: Required when the move pauses. Say what it waits on. on: person | agent | external | thing | decision | date | nobody. ref: who or what ('person:<id>', 'company:<id>', a label). reason: why. until: { date: ISO } resumes on that day; { moves: '<entity|track|focus_session>:<id>', to?: status or category } resumes when that thing moves; a dev fact: 'pr:<owner/name>#<n>' resumes when that pull request merges (to: 'closed' = when it is closed without merging); 'main:<owner/name>' when that repo's main is green again; 'job:<devbox job name>' when that devbox job finishes (to: 'passed' | 'failed' = only that verdict); a wait on the person: 'answer:<session id>/<slot key or label>' resumes when the person answers that slot (of a session you own); 'proposal:<proposal id>' when that proposal (filed under a session you own) is no longer pending (to sleep until the person answers your ask). reviewBy: an ISO date to look again (14 days by default when nothing resumes it on a date). Leave it out when the move does not pause.

occurredAt.description: When the move really happened, if earlier than now (ISO date-time): at most 30 days back, never in the future. The move is recorded now and marked backdated.

documentId.description: Attach this EXISTING document (its id) as the entity's body — e.g. re-attach a document whose entity lost it. Not for new text: use `content` or synap_create_document.

replaceBody.description: Set true with documentId when the entity ALREADY has a body and you mean to replace it (it is kept, detached, and comes back on undo). Without it the call is refused naming the current body. Always a proposal.

homeWorkspaceId.description: File a POD-WIDE record (one in no space) for this space, its home: the space's members and its apps then read it. Refused on a record that lives in a space (move it instead) and unless the person can write in that space. Always a proposal for you; undo puts the previous home back. null clears the home.

reasoning.description: Why you are making this write, in the person's words — shown to the human who reviews it. One line.

sessionId.description: OPTIONAL focus-session override. Leave it out and the write is attributed automatically — you do NOT normally pass this. Send it ONLY to disambiguate: when two or more of your focus sessions are open, automatic attribution deliberately declines rather than guess, and this is the only way to say which session the write belongs to. Also the way to JOIN a session another conversation started — automatic attribution never shares one across conversations. A session that isn't yours is ignored, not an error.

tools.name: synap_update_entities
tools.description: Change up to 500 existing entities in ONE call — retitles, property fixes, status moves. Use it for any change set; never script many single updates or Hub REST calls. Each item is {id, patch, expected?}; patch fields: title, description, properties, deleteProperties, expectedStatus (no kind change, no body — use synap_update_entity / synap_update_document for those). Governance is per item: each is written now (when it would auto-approve), or collected into ONE review for the person, or denied, or skipped (not found, changed since you read it, nothing to change). The answer lists applied, proposed {proposalId, count, reviewUrl}, denied, skipped, plus items[] with each verdict — a partial result is normal. 'proposed' is success: do not resend those items; a skipped item with `deferred: true` was held with today's writes past your daily limit and is replayed for you once approved. Pass validate:true first to see the verdicts without writing. Pass an idempotencyKey so a retried call returns the first answer instead of acting twice.

properties.description: Partial properties to merge into the entity.

expectedStatus.description: When the patch moves the status: the status you SAW. If it moved meanwhile the item is skipped.

hold.description: Required when the move pauses. tools.name: synap_create_document
tools.description: Create a Document: text to read or write (spec, memo, brief, research, notes, a status read-out, a report's source); a dashboard to monitor is a bento (synap_create_view), not a document of embeds. THREE modes: (1) markdown — `content`, with live embeds (:::synap-view, :::synap-entity, :::synap-cell). (2) a link — `url` (no `content`) for a file or page you have a LINK to but no bytes (a Google Doc, a PDF URL). (3) an HTML artifact — `type: "html"`, `content` a whole page to present or share outside the pod (a report: markdown first, its HTML generated from it). Pod admin RUNS it at `/open/<id>` in an isolated frame (scripts run; no network, so inline every script, style, font and image: no CDN; pod data only through the read-only bridge `window.synap.query(op, params)`, on the ops it declares in `reads`; at most 2 MB, a bigger page shows as source only). The receipt's `warnings` name what will not run. A page is not taken with `url` (send it as `content`) or `entityId` (an entity body is read as markdown): attach it with `attachTo`. Pass `entityId` to make it an existing entity's BODY: an entity has ONE body, so when it already has one the call is REFUSED before anything is written (`replaceBody: true` replaces it on purpose). A RELATED document is its own entity, linked with synap_link_entities. Also creating the entity? Prefer synap_create_entity with `content` (one call). Real file bytes: `synap_store_file` (≤10MB inline; bigger: `synap_request_upload`, then `synap_store_file({uploadToken})`). Attachment only happens when the document auto-approved; a proposal-gated one has no row to link yet, and the response says so. Needs the person's decision? Embed a `:::synap-ask` block, not a prose question (synap_load_skill("system/synap/document-embeds")).

type.description: What `content` is. "markdown" (default) is a document. "html" is a page pod admin runs at `/open/<id>` in an isolated frame: inline only (the policy blocks the network: no CDN, no remote font or image), at most 2 MB, reading pod data through the read-only bridge. The receipt's `warnings` say what will not run. Not taken with `url` or `entityId`.

entityId.description: Optional UUID of an EXISTING entity whose BODY this document becomes. The attach is a separate governed entity update — its own outcome comes back under `attached`. Refused when the entity already has a body (the refusal names it), unless `replaceBody` is true.

Also the way to JOIN a session another conversation started — automatic attribution never shares one across conversations. A session that isn't yours is ignored, not an error.

Never put a scope in a cell's props: the host stamps this one on every cell. Refused when it names something you cannot read.

tools.name: synap_update_document
tools.description: Edit a document with ops — a section, a passage, an addition — instead of rewriting it. Read it first with synap_get_document and pass its `revision` as `baseRevision`. Ops, applied in order: `upsert_section {id, title, body}` writes ONE `::::synap-section` block by id (replaces your own `ai` section, or appends a new one); `replace_text {old, new}` — `old` must match EXACTLY once, copy it from the document and include enough context (0 or 2+ matches is refused with the count); `append {body}`; `replace_all {content}` (whole body — needs baseRevision, always goes to review); `set_title {title}` renames the document (its one title — a human name, never an id), governed like the other ops; `insert_embed {directive, ref, props?, fallback?, sectionId?|after?}` adds an embed (synap-cell {cellKey} + props, synap-entity {id}, synap-view {viewId}) written for you — never hand-write directive text — at the end, at the end of section `sectionId`, or after the line holding `after`; `set_scope {scope}` sets the living document's scope (same shape as synap_create_document's, null clears it); `set_refresher {automationId}` binds the automation whose runs refresh its AI sections (null unbinds); `replace_block {blockId, html}` (html page) replaces the one element whose `data-block-id` (or slide id) is blockId; the rest stays. Refused: changing a section whose owner is `human` (by any op), and removing an embed unless `allow_removing_embeds: true`. Usually returns 'proposed' (the person reviews a per-section before/after); a governance rule may apply it directly. The response carries `preview` and `diagnostics` (embeds that will not render, each with a `fix` — advisory, never a refusal). A 'changed after you read it' error means re-read and redraft. Needs the person's decision? Embed a `:::synap-ask` block, not a prose question (synap_load_skill("system/synap/document-embeds")).

tools.name: synap_define_kind
tools.description: Define a new entity KIND — AND the door for ADDING A FIELD to a kind that already exists. It is SLUG-IDEMPOTENT: re-call it with an EXISTING slug and it returns that profile and adds only the `properties[]` that are not there yet (an existing field reports status 'unchanged' and is never rewritten — with ONE exception: re-declare an existing field with its `constraints.enum` PLUS new values to ADD allowed values. Governed like any schema change, and refused for the kind's status field and for a value one typo away from an allowed one (send the allowed one instead). This is the door when a write was refused because no allowed value fits). So to add `wedge_stage` to `question`, call this with slug 'question' and just that one field — there is NO separate add-property tool, and schema editing is NOT browser-only. A field takes `valueType`, `constraints` (an enum of allowed values lives here), `defaultValue`, `required`, and `overlay: true` to add it as a WORKSPACE OVERLAY instead of a base field on the kind — which is what you want for a field that only one domain should see, on a pod-wide kind like note/task/question. Call list_profiles + extend-first (load_skill system/synap-schema/extend-first) BEFORE minting a new slug. A hat on an existing kind — including item, task, deal — is a ROLE (synap_define_role / attach_facet), never a sibling kind. Prefer parentProfileSlug of the closest parent over a disconnected slug. A relationship-with-its-own-life (buyer×seller×price×stage) is its own kind (deal *precedent*), not a twin of CRM deal. POD-WIDE default. Slugs are NORMALISED to lowercase words joined by '-' (social_account_audit → social-account-audit, botScore → botscore): the result's `notice`/`normalized` names every rewrite — use the stored slugs in code and later calls. Governed: 'proposed' is success; a NEW kind's `properties` ride that same proposal (one approval creates the kind and its fields, so do not re-call for them). Creates it on this pod only; an official template is written in the catalog (synap-app/packages/workspace-templates); landing it on app-bases main publishes it.

tools.name: synap_orient
tools.description: The session BRIEFING — call first in every session. Leads with `startHere`: proposals you or your agents filed that await review (raise these first; the user's queue may hold more from others), open work sessions, the open goals they serve, each with where it stands (`openGoals`: file work into one with trackId), the most-used kinds, runnable actions, and the skill to load for concept depth. An agent key also gets `handedToYou`: the sessions the person handed to it (never one it started itself), then the ones that went stale in the last 7 days, marked `resume` with `quietSince` — continue that conversation, never start it fresh. `yourTools` says which tools this key lists, what synap_ask is for, and the exact synap_load_skill call that unlocks more. Then your identity, what is known about the user, projects (commitments, each spanning workspaces) and the workspaces (operational domains) that hold data. Pass scope:['projects'] and/or workspaceId to narrow — and PIN a `workspaceId` and orient also returns that space's `brief`: what it is FOR (purpose, persona), the kinds it HOLDS, its rules, its SKILLS (the agent know-how this space activates — each `{ slug, mode, when? }`; `mode:'always'` is in effect now, `'on-demand'` when the task matches its `when`), plus its playbooks and anchors. That is the one door to 'what is this space for, and what does it know' — an unpinned orient carries no brief. Light omits empty domains and the full type inventory; detail:'full' adds every workspace, descriptions, onboarding specs and per-workspace profiles. Every kind and role: synap_list_profiles.
