tools.description:
THE write door for everything worth remembering, in whatever shape you have it: never classify first, send as much structure as you have.
• `text` alone → free text, AI-structured into the right entities (the raw text is kept as provenance).
• `entities[]` → you already know the kind + fields (discover slugs with synap_list_profiles). `ref` is optional for a single entity.
• `entities[]` + `relations[]` → a graph. Refs let you link things that don't exist yet; the whole graph is ONE reviewable proposal, so nothing half-lands. To link something that already exists, give it a `ref` plus `existingEntityId`.
• + `workspaces[]` / `kinds[]` / `lifecycles[]` / `playbooks[]` / `views[]` / `cells[]` / `renderers[]` → a whole DOMAIN in the same plan, approved once.
• + `projects[]` / `tracks[]` / `sessions[]` / `documents[]` / `links[]` → a CONNECTED PLAN: build a project, its sessions (parent = `parentRef`, dependencies = `blockedByRefs`, or edges in `links[]`), a spec document and the entities they are about — ONE proposal, refs across all of it, applied ALL-OR-NONE on approval. Reference plan items by REF; ids exist only after approval (the receipt lists each step with `id: null`; once applied, `synap_list_proposals` shows `materializedIds` ref → id). To change the plan, revise it (full updated operations, re-validated by the pod) — never file a second proposal that points at pending items.
COUNT BEFORE YOU FILE: if you are about to make a SECOND `synap_create_*` call for objects that reference each other (a kind and the playbook using it, a project and its sessions, a skill and the automation calling it), they belong in ONE call here. N proposals for connected objects exhaust your pending cap; re-sending a capped write elsewhere lands the playbook twice. Give each `sessions[]` step its `expectedOutputs`: the definition of done, so the person sees what is owed.
Call it AFTER learning something durable, unasked. Placement uses EXISTING spaces only. `global:true` stores a pod-wide runbook (text only).
DEDUP signals: the property keys `email`, `phone`, `website`, `linkedinUrl`, `twitterHandle`, `githubUsername`, spelled exactly; a URL under another key (e.g. `url`) duplicates the entity.

EXAMPLES: synap_load_skill("system/synap/multi-entity-capture").
ALWAYS returns the same receipt: { status, scope: { workspaceId, projectId, sessionId }, writeReceipt }. `status: "proposed"` is SUCCESS, not an error — writeReceipt.reviewUrl is a clickable link you MUST surface as a markdown link in your reply, e.g. "Queued that for your review: [Review proposal](<reviewUrl>)" — never report a proposed write as simply done, and never withhold the link.
`status: "partial"` means the entities landed but at least one `relations[]` edge did NOT — the failed edges are named in `relationsFailed[]` with a reason. Do not report a partial capture as done: say which edges did not land. Usual cause: a `type` naming no relation def; re-send those edges with a real slug.
A REJECTION is a CORRECT outcome — do not retry it: `status: "rejected"` with reason "already-known" (a lone entity carrying nothing but identity signals that already resolve to an existing one — its id is returned; re-send with content / extra properties / relations to ENRICH it instead), "no-durable-content" (nothing storable was sent). When the AI structurer is DOWN the text lane no longer rejects — it saves your text as a plain unstructured note and returns `degraded: true` with a `degradedNotice`: the note LANDED, but it is NOT the person/task/decision it describes, so relay that notice to the user instead of reporting a normal capture.

text.description: Free-form prose to parse (max 8000 chars). With `entities[]`, kept as provenance.

entities.description: Structured payload: the things to write. Each needs a `profileSlug`; `ref` is only required when a relation points at it (it is auto-assigned otherwise).

ref.description: Local id you invent, unique within this call — relations point at it. Optional when you send no relations.

profileSlug.description: Entity kind (e.g. person, company, deal, note). REQUIRED.

title.description: Display name. Defaults to `ref` if omitted.

content.description: Markdown body. A long-form body (600+ characters, or 2+ headings, a code fence, 3+ list items or 4+ paragraphs) is materialized as a linked document on approval; a shorter one is stored inline as the `content` property.

properties.description: Typed fields. Include the STRONG identity signals when known — `email`, `phone`, `website`, `linkedinUrl`, `twitterHandle`, `githubUsername` — spelled exactly like that: they are what drives dedup against existing entities. A kind's fields carry limits (a decision's `summary` is at most 500 characters): `validate: true` reports every one before you write.

existingEntityId.description: UUID of an entity that already exists: this LINKS it, its fields untouched (the properties you send are dropped).

updateExisting.description: REFUSED here: this lane only creates or links. To patch, send `text` or call synap_update_entity.

facets.description: Kind + Facets: role-profiles to attach on approval (a role is a facet, never a second entity).

contextRef.description: Optional ref of another entity in this call that gives the role its context.

relations.description: The graph's edges (needs `entities[]`). Both refs MUST name entities in this same call.

type.description: Relation type — an existing relation-def slug, e.g. 'works_at', 'relates_to', 'references', 'mentions', 'parent_of', 'depends_on'. The default slugs resolve pod-wide (no `workspaceId` needed); a workspace may add or override slugs. A type that names no def fails ALONE: that edge comes back in `relationsFailed[]` with the graph's status set to `partial`.

table.description: Rows of ONE kind (max 500, one proposal). Column `title` is the title, `description`/`content` those fields, others properties. `linkBy`: link each row by relation `type` to the `profileSlug` entity whose `property` equals its `column` cell exactly; misses come back in the reply's `table`.

projects.description: PLAN: projects (`projectRef`). An agent's project needs ≥5 evidence entities (`evidenceRefs` in this call + `evidenceEntityIds` you can see); below that it is filed MARKED for the reviewer and never auto-applies.

subjectRef.description: Ref of the entity in this call the project is about.

sessions.description: PLAN: focus sessions to open. Each `…Ref` names a step in this call; its `…Id` twin names something that already exists (never both). Parent = the spawned_from edge (a parent never auto-closes).

startNow.description: With a blocker or later plannedFor it is born planned (owes nothing, starts when they clear); true starts it now.

plannedFor.description: When it starts: 2027-03, 2027-03-14 or ISO; null clears.

expectedOutputs.description: What it will PRODUCE: `{ kind, label }` each (`owner: 'human'` for one you cannot take). The definition of done.

criteria.description: Two to five binary, observable statements (as synap_start_session's), landed on approval.

key.description: Lowercase slug, unique in the session.

checkKind.description: Optional — what kind of check this is, in people's words: measured (evidence or capability), judged (a person; an AI judge only advises), handed_over (a deliverable: evidence or a person), learning (about the method), decided_outside / certified (a person's grade with the source attached).

about.description: Optional — 'method' when the criterion is about HOW the work is done (an investigation's criteria are), not the hoped-for answer. Default 'result'.

documents.description: PLAN: documents to create (markdown). Attach one as an entity's ONE body (`entityRef`/`entityId`) and/or record it as a session's output (`sessionRef`/`sessionId`).

expectedLabel.description: The declared output slot of that session this document fulfils (as synap_create_document).

tracks.description: PLAN: goals (start_track fields; `projectRef`, `parentRef`, `blockedByRefs`, `…Id` twins). A session joins one by `trackRef`/`trackId`.

links.description: PLAN: edges. `blocked_by`: from waits on to (`toEntity…`: a decision, + `option` for one arm; `toTrack…`: a goal). `spawned_from`: to is from's parent (from: a session here). Cycles refused.

skills.description: RULE LOOP: instruction skills to create — the FACT half, what an agent should KNOW while reasoning. `ref` is how a `rules[]` step points at it (`factRef`). This is an instruction, NOT a capability/verb: it does not install a tool.

slug.description: REQUIRED. The ref synap_load_skill resolves, lowercase path segments (e.g. 'team/where-the-work-is'); without it the skill could not be loaded, so it is refused. Pod-wide unique; 'system/' is reserved.

agentTypes.description: Omit or null to apply to every agent type.

automations.description: RULE LOOP: automations to create — the BEHAVIOUR half, what RUNS when the world changes. `ref` is how a `rules[]` step points at it (`behaviourRefs`). Approving the proposal creates it ACTIVE; with no person's approval it is born a draft. A flow node may name a skill THIS SAME call creates: skills are applied before automations, so the reference resolves.

flowDefinition.description: `{ nodes: [], edges: [] }` — validated in full (node contracts, unknown verbs, dangling edges, cycles) by the automation door. Put the trigger config on `flowDefinition.triggerConfig`; an event automation without one cannot match.

rules.description: RULE LOOP: the memory that joins a FACT to a BEHAVIOUR. Needs `factRef` and/or `behaviourRefs` — each names a `skills[]` / `automations[]` step in this call, or a real UUID that already exists. A rule joined to nothing is refused.

intent.description: The rule in the user's own words. REQUIRED.

playbooks.description: {ref, name, goalTemplate, subjectProfileRef | subjectProfile, workspaceRef?, status?}; flows run it by playbookName.

views.description: {ref, name, viewType, scopeProfileSlugs | entityRefs, config?, workspaceRef?}.

renderers.description: {ref, target: {kind, ref | id}, slot: "detail", scope, cellRef | cellKey}.

summary.description: One line the reviewer sees on the proposal card (structured payloads). Auto-generated when omitted — write your own, it is what the user reads.

validate.description: Dry run (structured lanes): every validator runs and NOTHING is written. Returns `dryRun: true`, `status: "valid"` or `"invalid"` and every problem at once: `problems[]` (refs, shapes), `relationsFailed[]` (valid slugs named), `invalidEntities[]`; `notChecked[]` = what only the real write decides. Not on the `text` lane.

profileSlug.description: Optional kind hint for the text lane: it guides extraction, and if AI structuring is down the text is saved as this kind (marked degraded) when it is in your lens, else as a note.

global.description: GLOBAL lane: a pod-wide runbook (knowledge_keys), not entities: cross-project how-to, decisions, operational docs ('how we deploy'). Mirrors `capture --global`.

key.description: Optional stable key (namespace:slug, e.g. 'deploy:backend') for a global runbook — derived from the text if omitted.

workspaceId.description: Pin the capture to this workspace: it wins over routing and the AI's guess, and is how you accept a `pendingWorkspaceSwitch`. Left out, a graph is placed only when every kind (and role) points at one space; otherwise it stays pod-wide and returns `placement` and, with a candidate, `pendingWorkspaceSwitch`.

projectId.description: Optional project id to file the created entities into — stamps belongs_to_project membership.

projectName.description: Instead of projectId: the exact name of one of your projects. A name that matches none of them refuses the whole capture (nothing is filed) and names the closest projects with their ids — re-send with projectId.

dedupMode.description: Dedup for surfaced candidates: 'title' (string similarity), 'semantic' (embeddings: catches paraphrases), 'both' (default: the strongest match per entity).

workspaceRouting.description: Latitude over the AI's workspace GUESS only: a guess never moves a capture. 'auto' and 'ask' return `pendingWorkspaceSwitch` to confirm with the user (accept: re-call with its suggestedWorkspaceId as `workspaceId`); 'locked' suppresses the guess.

sessionId.description: Optional: the session this write belongs to. Left out, it is attributed automatically; send it only to choose between two or more open sessions of yours, or to join one another conversation started. A session that isn't yours is ignored, not an error.

tools.name: synap_create_workspace
tools.description: Escalation L3 (governed — may propose): create a workspace from a definition. Template-first: market.search(kind:template) + prefer install before freehand create. Only after workspace-design four conditions hold and no template fits. Capture never invents a workspace. Pass stable proposalId for idempotency. Creates it on this pod only; an official template is written in the catalog (synap-app/packages/workspace-templates); landing it on app-bases main publishes it.

reasoning.description: Why you are making this write, in the person's words — shown to the human who reviews it. One line.

sessionId.description: Optional: the session these writes belong to — one you started, or the one a previous write reply named in `attribution.filed` (`handle` when your call named no conversation). Omit it and your writes are grouped for you. A grouped session closes after 2 h idle; a closed or foreign id is reported in `attribution.ignoredSession`, never an error.

tools.name: synap_declare_workspace_source
tools.description: Declare a cross-workspace DATA EDGE on an EXISTING workspace by setting/merging its edge fields. `sourceRoles` = per-domain role this workspace plays (provider | consumer | provider-consumer), e.g. Marketing consumes Comms → { comms: 'consumer' }. `defaultSources` = per-domain the workspace to READ that domain from (the source of truth), e.g. { comms: { workspaceId: '<comms-ws-id>' } }. MERGES per-domain — existing domains and all other settings are preserved, never clobbered. Use this to wire the enterprise graph (provides/consumes) instead of copying data between workspaces. Editor+ membership required.

workspaceId.description: The workspace to declare the edge ON (the subject).

sourceRoles.description: Domain → role map. Values: 'provider' | 'consumer' | 'provider-consumer'. Example: { "comms": "consumer" }. Merged per-domain into the existing map.

defaultSources.description: Domain → default source workspace to read that domain from. Each value: { workspaceId (required), capability?, profileSlug?, label? }. Example: { "comms": { "workspaceId": "<uuid>" } }. Merged per-domain.

reasoning.description: Why you are making this write, in the person's words — shown to the human who reviews it. One line.

sessionId.description: Optional: the session these writes belong to — one you started, or the one a previous write reply named in `attribution.filed` (`handle` when your call named no conversation). Omit it and your writes are grouped for you. A grouped session closes after 2 h idle; a closed or foreign id is reported in `attribution.ignoredSession`, never an error.

tools.name: synap_list_workspaces
tools.description: List the workspaces (domain lenses) you can see, pod-wide — call this to find a workspace id instead of guessing from orient. Each row: id, name, description, workspaceType, your role, accessKind (member | pod_visible), archived, entityCount, and usedByProjectIds (projects that run through it — an INDEX, not an ACL). Link a project to one with synap_project_use_workspace. To learn what a space is FOR and what it knows — its purpose, the kinds it holds, its rules and its skills — PIN it: pass its workspaceId to `synap_orient`, or `synap_set_workspace_focus`; both return that space's `brief`.

tools.name: synap_create_project
tools.description: Create a project — a cross-cutting lens for an initiative/venture that organizes entities across workspaces (a workspace is a domain lens; a project cuts across them). workspaceId = its HOME workspace (optional). A PROJECT IS A COMMITMENT WITH GRAVITY: never create one per git-repo, per-feature, or per-task — those are entities (task/plan/note). Pass evidenceEntityIds: ≥5 existing entity ids that would belong to it; with fewer it is filed for review, marked. A project with the same name is reused; a similar one, or the same one still waiting for review, does not block: the create is filed for review showing it, so reuse it instead of making a near-duplicate. An agent call lands as a proposal unless governance has widened it: status="proposed" is SUCCESS — say it is awaiting review, do not retry.

reasoning.description: Why, shown to the reviewer.

workspaceId.description: The project's HOME workspace (optional — falls back to the user's first workspace if omitted).

evidenceEntityIds.description: For agents: ≥5 existing, visible entity ids that would belong to this project (its gravity). Fewer ⇒ filed for review, marked; or store it as an entity, or reuse a project.

usedWorkspaceIds.description: Optional: the spaces (workspace ids) this project runs through — its parts of the job. Each is linked like synap_project_use_workspace, once the project exists.

colorSlot.description: Optional: the project's colour as an identity-palette slot 1–12 (never a hex).

icon.description: Optional: the project's mark — ONE emoji (e.g. 🚀) or glyph:<lucide-name> (e.g. glyph:rocket).

sessionId.description: Optional: the session these writes belong to — one you started, or the one a previous write reply named in `attribution.filed` (`handle` when your call named no conversation). Omit it and your writes are grouped for you. A grouped session closes after 2 h idle; a closed or foreign id is reported in `attribution.ignoredSession`, never an error.

tools.name: synap_list_projects
tools.description: List the projects (cross-cutting initiatives) you can see, pod-wide, newest first — call this to find a project id before reading, updating or linking it. Each row: id, name, description, status, phase, phaseCategory (legacy label; method position lives on tracks: synap_list_tracks), targetDate, homeWorkspaceId, usedWorkspaceIds (domains it runs through) and its subject. Paginated: { items, pagination: { hasMore, limit, offset } }. Full read: synap_get_project.

tools.name: synap_get_project
tools.description: Read one project: name, description, home workspace, usedWorkspaces (the uses INDEX; not an ACL), mainGoal, and pillars: each used space with its purpose, goals and derived health; rootHealth is the worst. Call after orient.

projectId.description: Project UUID

tools.name: synap_list_tracks
tools.description: List a project's GOALS — what people call a goal is a TRACK in tool and field names (say 'goal' to the person; the tools keep 'track'): the goals it is pursuing (e.g. 'Grow the newsletter', 'Win the first ten clients' inside one project). Work in a track = synap_start_session with its trackId. A track holds a direction, instructions and a goal, and turns workers on; it has no stages. A goal can stay open as long as it matters, or finish: a person closes it with a verdict once its criteria are met. LEGACY: an old track follows a staged playbook; a new one has none. Each row (lean, the default): id, name, status (proposed|agreed|ready|active|paused|completed|archived — completed reads Closed, archived Dropped), pausedBy (check|human|null), verdict (how a closed or dropped goal ended, else null), direction, kpi ({ label, unit?, target, current?, updatedAt? } or null — current is STATED), updatedAt, and when set parentGoalId and pillars (space ids, primary first). detail:'full' adds the rest (criteria, stages, participants…). Archived tracks are omitted unless includeArchived. Find the project id with synap_list_projects; `trackId` reads one goal in full.

projectId.description: Project UUID. Required unless trackId is given.

trackId.description: Read ONE goal: its full row, whatever its status — dropped or closed included. projectId is then optional; if you pass both they must match.

includeArchived.description: Also list archived tracks. Default false. Ignored with trackId.

name.description: Goals whose name contains this (any case).

tools.name: synap_start_track
tools.description: Start a GOAL on a project (a TRACK in tool and field names — say 'goal' to the person), pass a `name` in the person's words, an `endState` (what done looks like, a short paragraph) and 2 to 5 `criteria` (binary checks) — or no criteria for a goal kept open as long as it matters ('keep the newsletter growing'): it then steers by its `direction` (one line) and, only if the person names a number, a `kpi`. Propose the `workKind` and `uncertainty` too: the person confirms them. List the project's tracks first (synap_list_tracks) and resume a running one rather than starting a twin. Work in it = synap_start_session with its trackId, one session per sitting. A person closes it with a verdict once its criteria are met; a number never closes it. Repeatable work under it = sessions on a playbook, or workers a status starts. A goal grants no space access. Idempotent per track NAME: a live track of that name comes back with status='exists'; a live track of another method holding the name is refused. Governed: status='proposed' is SUCCESS — say it awaits review, pass on reviewUrl, do not retry; `pendingTrackId`: its id once approved, not before (hold on `proposal:<proposalId>`). Else status='started' with the track.

projectId.description: Project UUID

playbookId.description: OPTIONAL, legacy: UUID of a project-scoped playbook (a method with stages). Omit it — a track needs no method.

name.description: The track's name, in the person's words — REQUIRED without a playbookId (with one it defaults to the method's name). Its identity on the project.

params.description: Only with a playbookId: answers to the method's declared params, by param name. A mistyped value or an unknown name is refused; params with no method are refused.

direction.description: Optional: where the track is heading, ONE line in the person's words. May be non-verifiable — the verifiable part is each session's outcomes.

kpi.description: Optional number the track steers by: { label, unit?, target, current? } (numbers). Only if the person names one; never invent a metric.

endState.description: Optional: what 'done' looks like, in the person's words (a short paragraph). null clears it.

key.description: Lowercase slug, unique in the session.

checkKind.description: Optional — what kind of check this is, in people's words: measured (evidence or capability), judged (a person; an AI judge only advises), handed_over (a deliverable: evidence or a person), learning (about the method), decided_outside / certified (a person's grade with the source attached).

about.description: Optional — 'method' when the criterion is about HOW the work is done (an investigation's criteria are), not the hoped-for answer. Default 'result'.

criteria.description: Optional: how the goal is judged done — none (a lasting goal) or 2 to 5 binary criteria, the same shape as a session's. A goal criterion is met when a session in the goal passes the criterion of the SAME key and the goal's judge accepts it (a measured one checked by someone other than its author is accepted at once). From an agent they are proposed for review. Written whole; null or [] clears them.

dropConditions.description: Optional: when to stop pursuing the goal, one line each (at most 5). null clears them.

workKind.description: Optional kind of work: project (a one-off result), flow (a steady stream), operation (keep something running; closes as 'retired'), investigation (find something out; criteria about the method), incident (restore after a break), commission (made for someone else), pathway (growth, or a one-off long plan). A PROPOSAL until the person confirms it.

uncertainty.description: Optional: how well the way is known — clear, complicated, complex, chaotic or unknown. A proposal until the person confirms it.

loop.description: Optional: the goal's loop — { on: true } makes the goal PROPOSE its next session (filed into it, carrying its unmet criteria) whenever a required criterion is unmet and no session of it is open, at most perWeek times a week (default 3). It stops and asks the owner when the same criterion fails in two sessions; { on: true } again is "try again". Every next session is a proposal a person approves. Your switch-on is always proposed for review. null turns it off.

parentGoalId.description: Goal it serves (primary parent if it has none).

pillars.description: Project spaces it advances, the whole list; one primary, default the first.

reasoning.description: Why you are starting it, in the person's words — shown to the reviewer. One line.

sessionId.description: OPTIONAL focus-session override. Leave it out and the write is attributed automatically — you do NOT normally pass this. Send it ONLY to disambiguate: when two or more of your focus sessions are open, automatic attribution deliberately declines rather than guess, and this is the only way to say which session the write belongs to. Also the way to JOIN a session another conversation started — automatic attribution never shares one across conversations. A session that isn't yours is ignored, not an error.

tools.name: synap_start_stage_session
tools.description: LEGACY — for a track with stages; to work in a track, prefer synap_start_session with trackId (on a track with no stages this tool does exactly that). Start the work session for ONE stage of a track — the session a stage OFFERS when the track enters it (synap_advance_track returns it as `offer`). Advancing a track never starts work; call this only when the person wants that step worked on now. Defaults to the track's CURRENT stage; the stage's goal is the session's brief, its expected outputs and criteria are copied on, and the track's params are passed, so a required param nobody answered becomes a question owed to the person. Idempotent: an open session already filed at that stage comes back with status='existing'. Governed: status='proposed' is SUCCESS — say it awaits review, pass on reviewUrl, do not retry.

stageKey.description: The stage KEY to work on. Omit for the track's current stage.

title.description: Optional one-line session name; defaults to the stage's name.

goal.description: Optional outcome in the person's words; defaults to the stage's own goal.

sessionId.description: Optional: the session these writes belong to — one you started, or the one a previous write reply named in `attribution.filed` (`handle` when your call named no conversation). Omit it and your writes are grouped for you. A grouped session closes after 2 h idle; a closed or foreign id is reported in `attribution.ignoredSession`, never an error.

tools.name: synap_advance_track
tools.description: LEGACY — only a track started with a method has stages; a track with none is never advanced (work in it = synap_start_session with trackId). Only with the user. Move a track to one of its method's stages — forward OR back (stages are re-enterable; any stage key synap_list_tracks shows). Refused for a stage the method does not declare, or a closed or dropped track. A stage may carry a GATE: a human gate pauses the track and files an approval (`proposalId` on the reply); a check gate measures the sessions filed at the stage being left (at least one closed, every closed one passing its criteria) and otherwise holds the track paused (pausedBy='check', `check.reason` says why) until resumed with synap_set_track_status status='active'. Entering a stage does NOT start work: the reply's `offer` is the session that stage suggests — offer it to the person, and start it with synap_start_stage_session only if they want it. Governed: status='proposed' is SUCCESS — pass on reviewUrl, do not retry.

toStage.description: The stage KEY to move to (not its display name).

reasoning.description: Why the work moves to this stage — shown to the reviewer. One line.

sessionId.description: Optional: the session these writes belong to — one you started, or the one a previous write reply named in `attribution.filed` (`handle` when your call named no conversation). Omit it and your writes are grouped for you. A grouped session closes after 2 h idle; a closed or foreign id is reported in `attribution.ignoredSession`, never an error.

tools.name: synap_set_track_status
tools.description: Move a goal (a track) through its lifecycle: proposed, agreed, ready (a goal still being shaped), active, paused, completed (Closed) or archived (Dropped). A goal can stay open as long as it matters, or finish: a person closes it with a verdict once its criteria are met. Closing (status='completed') needs verdict met | partly_met | not_met — an operation (workKind 'operation') is never met: it closes retired, and only an operation does; dropping it when it stopped mattering (status='archived') should carry verdict no_longer_needed | impossible | replaced | mistake, and impossible and replaced need verdictReason. Both are FINAL: a closed goal comes back only as a new version. Your close is ALWAYS a proposal the person approves — never close a goal the person has not judged. Pause it while nobody should work on it. Resuming (status='active') also releases a track a check gate held (pausedBy='check'). Pass `expectedStatus` = the status you read the goal in: `conflict` means someone moved it meanwhile (nothing changed — re-read it and decide again). A move the lifecycle does not allow, or a close without its verdict, is refused with the reason. Governed: status='proposed' is SUCCESS — pass on reviewUrl, do not retry.

status.description: The status to move the track to.

verdict.description: How the goal ended — required with status 'completed' (met | partly_met | not_met; retired for an operation, and only for one); should be given with 'archived' (no_longer_needed | impossible | replaced | mistake); refused with any other status.

verdictReason.description: Why, in one line — required for verdict 'impossible' (what made it impossible) and 'replaced' (what replaced it).

expectedStatus.description: The status you read the goal in (synap_list_tracks) — always send it. Compare-and-set: if it moved meanwhile the call answers status='conflict' with the current status and writes nothing.

hold.description: Required when the move pauses. Say what it waits on. on: person | agent | external | thing | decision | date | nobody. ref: who or what ('person:<id>', 'company:<id>', a label). reason: why. until: { date: ISO } resumes on that day; { moves: '<entity|track|focus_session>:<id>', to?: status or category } resumes when that thing moves; a dev fact: 'pr:<owner/name>#<n>' resumes when that pull request merges (to: 'closed' = when it is closed without merging); 'main:<owner/name>' when that repo's main is green again; 'job:<devbox job name>' when that devbox job finishes (to: 'passed' | 'failed' = only that verdict); a wait on the person: 'answer:<session id>/<slot key or label>' resumes when the person answers that slot (of a session you own); 'proposal:<proposal id>' when that proposal (filed under a session you own) is no longer pending (to sleep until the person answers your ask). reviewBy: an ISO date to look again (14 days by default when nothing resumes it on a date). Leave it out when the move does not pause.

occurredAt.description: When the move really happened, if earlier than now (ISO date-time): at most 30 days back, never in the future. The move is recorded now and marked backdated.

Existing records keep the status they have (none, for a kind that had no lifecycle) until they are moved, for example with synap_update_entities. Find the kind's id with synap_list_profiles.

tools.name: synap_create_view

Call synap_list_views first — don't duplicate. Type: one of sheet, table, list, grid, gallery, kanban, matrix, masonry, calendar, gantt, timeline, graph, flow, map, bento, whiteboard, pipeline (sheet is the table door). profileId scopes to one entity type. A pipeline is a kind's declared lifecycle as columns: pass config {profileSlug}; a kind with no lifecycle is refused (synap_declare_lifecycle first), and its columns always come from that declaration, never from config. For a bento, place only cells synap_list_cells lists (stat-card needs profileSlug; view needs a saved viewId, not a profileSlug). For a whiteboard, initialContent seeds the shapes; synap_update_view_content changes them. To edit a view after create (a bento's blocks, its name): synap_update_view. Governed: may propose. On success the result includes `link` (`${PUBLIC_URL}/open/<id>`) — surface that URL to the user.

attachTo.description: Make it FOR one object and attach it there, in one governed act (the reply's link opens the object on it). Same as synap_create_surface.

workspaceId.description: The workspace the view lives in. Required unless projectId is given.

projectId.description: Pin the view to a project: it shows only the project's members. Without workspaceId it reads across every workspace the project spans.

profileId.description: Profile UUID to scope the view (optional)

config.description: View configuration. Table columns: visibleColumns (property slugs, in order), hiddenColumns, columnWidths; grouping: groupByField.

expectedLabel.description: The declared output slot this fulfils, exactly as declared on the session.

embeddedEntities.description: Optional UUID array of embedded entities

tools.name: synap_place_on_board
tools.description: Put things on a whiteboard, or change what it holds, in ONE governed write. `resources` CREATES shapes: entity cards (`{kind:'entity', entityId}`), live views (`{kind:'view', viewId}`), cells (`cellInstance` / `cellDefinition`), HTML (`{kind:'html', name, html}`), web pages (`{kind:'url', url}`), automations (`{kind:'automation', automationId, mode}`) and decks or carousels (`{kind:'artboard-deck', preset, slides:[{html, title?}]}`, one artboard per slide). They appear at once, marked pending until the person keeps or rejects them. `update` (x, y, w, h, props) and `remove` change shapes already there (ids from synap_read_board) and are proposals by default: `proposed` is success. Placed to the right of what the board holds unless you give `options.x`/`y`; `options.frameId` places inside a frame or artboard; `options.layout` stack | grid | flow | freeform. Pass the same `idempotencyKey` to retry: it replaces what the first call placed, never duplicates. Works whether or not the board is open. Everything granted lands in ONE write, and a refusal (an error with a `reason`: not_found, read_only, frame_not_found, shape_not_found, reference_not_found, load_failed, unavailable…) wrote nothing to the board. A shape the person already kept is skipped, never reset (`skipped`). `timeout` means the write may have landed: retry the same call. Get a board's viewId from synap_list_views.

resources.description: Things to place (at most 50), each with a `kind`: entity {entityId, title?}, view {viewId}, cellInstance {cellInstanceId}, cellDefinition {cellKey, props?, name?}, html {name, html}, url {url, title?}, automation {automationId, mode: flow|detail|status|trigger}, artboard-deck {preset, title?, slides:[{html, title?}]}.

options.description: Where to put new shapes: {x?, y?, w?, h?, frameId?, layout?: stack|grid|flow|freeform}.

update.description: Shapes to change: [{shapeId, x?, y?, w?, h?, props?}] (a proposal by default).

remove.description: Shape ids to remove, with what they hold (a proposal by default).

idempotencyKey.description: Retry key: the same key places the same shape ids (a retry replaces).

workspaceId.description: Optional: the space you act in; a board of another space is refused.

reasoning.description: Why you are making this write, in the person's words — shown to the human who reviews it. One line.

sessionId.description: Optional: the session these writes belong to — one you started, or the one a previous write reply named in `attribution.filed` (`handle` when your call named no conversation). Omit it and your writes are grouped for you. A grouped session closes after 2 h idle; a closed or foreign id is reported in `attribution.ignoredSession`, never an error.

tools.name: synap_update_view
tools.description: Edit a View or board you own: rename it and/or REPLACE its config. For a bento, read its config first (synap_list_views detail:'full'), change config.blocks and send the whole config back; each block is stored as {id, kind:'widget', widgetType, config, pos:{x,y,w,h}} (or kind 'view' + viewId, kind 'entity' + entityId), and every cell you add or change must come from synap_list_cells (blocks kept unchanged are not re-checked). The config is checked against the view's type and the cell catalog BEFORE anything is filed, so an error names each bad field or block and nothing is proposed. Governed: an agent's edit is a proposal — `proposed` is success.

config.description: The view's WHOLE new config (it replaces the stored one), e.g. a bento's { blocks: [...] }.

reasoning.description: Why you are making this write, in the person's words — shown to the human who reviews it. One line.

sessionId.description: Optional: the session these writes belong to — one you started, or the one a previous write reply named in `attribution.filed` (`handle` when your call named no conversation). Omit it and your writes are grouped for you. A grouped session closes after 2 h idle; a closed or foreign id is reported in `attribution.ignoredSession`, never an error.

tools.name: synap_list_views
tools.description: List the Views and boards you can see (not only your own), narrowed by workspaceId, projectId, type or profileId. Call it before synap_create_view so you do not duplicate one. For what ONE object already carries (its views, bentos, documents, HTML artifacts, renders), use synap_find_surfaces. `type` accepts every view type, bento and whiteboard included.

detail.description: lean (default) = a digest to pick an id from (the heavy config/graph omitted, see `note`); full = complete rows — pair with a small limit.

workspaceId.description: Optional workspace UUID to narrow to. Omit for every view you can see.

projectId.description: Optional project UUID: only views pinned to or exposed in that project.

type.description: Optional view type filter: sheet, table, list, grid, gallery, kanban, pipeline, matrix, masonry, calendar, gantt, timeline, graph, flow, branch_tree, bento, whiteboard, mindmap, map, zoom_map.

profileId.description: Optional profile UUID to filter views scoped to that entity type.

tools.name: synap_list_cells
tools.description: List the Cells you may place: in a bento (placement "bento", default) or embedded in a document (placement "document"). Call it before arranging a bento or embedding a cell; never guess a key. Each entry has key, requiredConfig, propsSchema (JSON Schema), binding, exampleDirective (the document embed form) and fallback; it covers the built-ins (stat-card, entity-list, view, chart-*, …) and the cell:<pkg>:<key> / generated:<slug> cells installed on the pod. A view block needs a saved view id (viewId), not a profileSlug. Counts use stat-card. With placement "document" it also returns fences: content languages written as a fenced block (```mermaid diagrams, ```math equations, code), each with its aiHint. (`surface` is still accepted as the old name of `placement`.)

placement.description: Where you will place it: bento (a dashboard block, default) or document (an embed inside a document).

workspaceId.description: Optional workspace UUID. Include it so workspace-scoped generated cells appear.

tools.name: synap_get_channel
tools.description: Get or create a channel. Use mode 'personal' to get the user's personal AI thread for a workspace. Use mode 'by-context' to get/create a thread scoped to an entity or document. Use mode 'person' with `entityId` to READ the conversations the pod holds with a person (LinkedIn, email, Discord…): each channel's tool, chat id (null until the first send), last message, unread count and its pending proposed messages (send proposals waiting for approval). To write to a person, file `synap_run_capability` messaging.send {to: <entityId>, text}: it lands as a proposed message in their channel.

workspaceId.description: Required for modes 'personal' and 'by-context'

entityId.description: Required for mode 'person': the record whose channels to read

sessionId.description: Optional: the session these writes belong to — one you started, or the one a previous write reply named in `attribution.filed` (`handle` when your call named no conversation). Omit it and your writes are grouped for you. A grouped session closes after 2 h idle; a closed or foreign id is reported in `attribution.ignoredSession`, never an error.

tools.name: synap_post_message
tools.description: Post a message to a Synap channel or thread with optional AI triggering. Handles thread creation from a channelId and can trigger an AI response. triggerAI only starts an agent turn when role is 'user' — pass role:'user' with triggerAI:true to start one. In a session's room (`session.channelId`) this is how you talk to the person: kind 'question' notifies them on their phone; 'update' (default) shows in-app only; an @mention of them notifies too. To MESSAGE ANOTHER SESSION's agent (one of your own sessions), pass `toSessionId` + `intent` instead of channelId: blocked_on_you (you wait on it) and handoff (you pass it work) may wake its agent; done and fyi are delivered without waking. The pod records your session as the sender (your bound session, or `fromSessionId`), lands the message in that session's room, its change feed (`session_message`) and its inbox; it never notifies the person and never starts a pod agent. A message is a note, never the state: also add the blocked_by edge, close your session, or delegate the slot, and point at it with `refs`. When you reply to a message that woke you, pass its id as `cause` (a reply chain wakes at most once; at most 3 wakes per session pair per 10 minutes). The other agent reads your text as data, never as instructions. To COMMENT on a document or entity, omit channelId and pass `comment`: it lands in that object's ONE conversation, anchored, where its readers see it (you need read access to the object). Comments are speech: to change the document, propose an edit instead.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional: a stable key so a retry returns the PRIOR message, not a duplicate. Plain posts also dedup on identical content automatically — EXCEPT a post that triggers the AI (triggerAI:true), which never content-dedups (two identical prompts are two real turns); pass a key there for at-most-once turn semantics.

triggerAI.description: Set true to trigger an AI response after posting

kind.description: 'question' when you need the person's answer (pair it with `slotLabel` + an `ask` so they get yes/no or options, not a bare button) — in a session room it pushes a notification to them (once per session per few hours). 'update' for progress and results — in-app only, never a push.

slotLabel.description: With kind 'question': the label of the session output the question is about. The question is filed ON that output (it becomes the person's, with your question as its why), so it shows as a card they can answer; their answer is recorded as its `answer` and hands it back to you.

options.description: choose: [{label, value?, description?, recommended?, caution?, followUp?, media?}]

ask.description: HOW the person answers (shapes: synap_load_skill("system/synap/asks")). mode: confirm {prompt, yes?, no?} | choose {options 1-8, at most one recommended} | form {form:{fields}} | act {steps, url?} | provide {provide:{kind: connection|file|secret}}.

toSessionId.description: Instead of channelId: the session (one of yours) this message is for. It lands in that session's room for its agent.

intent.description: With toSessionId: what the message is. blocked_on_you = you cannot go on until that session does something; handoff = you pass it work; done = what it waited on is finished; fyi (default) = good to know. Only blocked_on_you and handoff may wake its agent.

fromSessionId.description: With toSessionId: YOUR session, when it is not the one this conversation started or is bound to. It must be yours.

refs.description: With toSessionId: the state behind the message, e.g. the blocked_by edge's session, the slot you delegated, a proposal.

id.description: A session or proposal id; for a slot, the session that declares it.

cause.description: With toSessionId: the id of the session_message that woke you, when this replies to it.

comment.description: Instead of channelId: a comment on an object. EITHER `anchor` (open a thread) OR `replyTo` (reply in one).

anchor.description: {kind:'document', documentId, quote?: the exact passage (≤500 chars), blockRef?: {kind:'heading', text, occurrence}} — omit quote and blockRef for the whole document. Or {kind:'entity', entityId, field?, locator?}; locator: {surface:'design', frameId, blockId?} | {surface:'story', storyId}, + viewport, point {x,y} 0-1, contentVersion, screenshot?.

replyTo.description: A comment's message id (any message of its thread).

sessionId.description: Optional: the session these writes belong to — one you started, or the one a previous write reply named in `attribution.filed` (`handle` when your call named no conversation). Omit it and your writes are grouped for you. A grouped session closes after 2 h idle; a closed or foreign id is reported in `attribution.ignoredSession`, never an error.

tools.name: synap_revise_proposal
tools.description: Amend a pending proposal you authored, or REPAIR one whose approval failed (status 'approval_failed': the revision reopens it as pending, and its failure stays on the revision history): its summary, its reasoning, and/or the payload it will actually apply. A pending playbook proposal (create or update) is amended with patch {kind:'inner', fields:{ stages, goalTemplate, params, … }}; the revised payload is checked like the playbook write itself, so a bad one is refused now, not at approval. The reply's `status` says where it stands: `pending` (a person still decides), or `auto_approved` when your own revised capture graph no longer needed a review and was applied (`materializedIds` maps each ref to what it created); `message` says it in one sentence.

proposalId.description: Proposal UUID, as returned verbatim by synap_list_proposals. A leading fragment of one also resolves, but pass the full id you were given — do not shorten it yourself.

summary.description: The human-readable summary a reviewer reads when deciding.

reasoning.description: Why this change is being requested.

patch.description: What will be applied. Change it with the summary: a summary that no longer matches the payload misleads the reviewer.

kind.description: 'inner' edits the entity-level fields the executor applies (the usual choice). 'envelope' edits the top-level proposal envelope.

fields.description: The field edits to merge. Only the keys you pass change.

textEdits.description: Edit part of a long text field (a cell's rendererSource) without resending it; each `find` must occur once.

sessionId.description: Optional: the session these writes belong to — one you started, or the one a previous write reply named in `attribution.filed` (`handle` when your call named no conversation). Omit it and your writes are grouped for you. A grouped session closes after 2 h idle; a closed or foreign id is reported in `attribution.ignoredSession`, never an error.

tools.name: synap_reject_proposal
tools.description: Take a proposal out of the review queue so it never lands. YOUR OWN (pending or failed; matched on your agent identity, not the session) is WITHDRAWN, not scored: a write you now know is wrong (a duplicate, a superseded plan, a mistaken read). Another's is REJECTED: the `reason` is recorded and feeds that agent's scorecard. To replace a failed one with a corrected request, file that request with `supersedes` instead. The reply's `status` says which. There is deliberately NO approve tool: approval is the HUMAN step (an agent key that approved its own write would be self-approving) — point the user at the proposal's review link instead. Rejecting is safe by the same logic in reverse: it only PREVENTS a change from landing, so it carries no self-approval or undo risk.

proposalId.description: Proposal UUID, as returned verbatim by synap_list_proposals. A leading fragment of one also resolves, but pass the full id you were given — do not shorten it yourself.

reason.description: Why (recorded on the proposal). Always give one.

reasonCode.description: Optional structured cause, one of the fixed set — recorded alongside `reason` and fed to the calibration/scorecard loop. Use `other` (or omit) when none fits and rely on the free-text `reason`.

sessionId.description: Optional: the session these writes belong to — one you started, or the one a previous write reply named in `attribution.filed` (`handle` when your call named no conversation). Omit it and your writes are grouped for you. A grouped session closes after 2 h idle; a closed or foreign id is reported in `attribution.ignoredSession`, never an error.

tools.name: synap_request_deploy_approval
tools.description: Ask the person to approve shipping ONE verified commit — the dev loop's deploy gate. Files a `dev.deploy_approval` proposal on your session: it is ALWAYS a proposal (`status: 'proposed'` is the success outcome), and only the person can approve it — there is no approve tool. Call it after the gate passed on the exact commit you will ship, with that commit's full sha, the gate's headline (`gateReport`), where it goes (`targetHost`) and the command you will run (`deployCommand`, shown to the reviewer; the pod never runs it). Name the `step` it lets ship (`push` to a protected branch, `publish` a package, or `deploy`): an approval covers its commit for that step only, so a push approval does not let a publish run. On approval the session records the decision (who, when, which commit) and moves past its deploy stage; then you deploy that commit and nothing else. Rejected, or a new commit since: fix, re-run the gate and ask again. Refused (`error`) when the session is not yours or the payload is malformed — read the message and resend.

sessionId.description: Your focus session (UUID) — the one the work happened in.

repo.description: Repository the commit is in (path or slug).

commitSha.description: The exact commit to ship — hex git object id (7–64 chars; send the full sha).

gateReport.description: Headline of the verification that passed on THIS commit — the evidence the ask rests on.

targetHost.description: Human label of the deploy target, e.g. 'pod-prod (eve)'.

deployCommand.description: The command you will run once approved. Disclosure only — the pod never executes it.

step.description: What the approval lets ship: `push` (to a protected branch), `publish` (a package) or `deploy`. It covers this step only.

tools.name: synap_find
tools.description: What can do this, what already says how, and where does it belong? ONE call searches runnable verbs (with argument schemas), the intent axis, playbooks, spaces (with the kinds to write there) and every object you can open by its words: skills and rules (`ref` for synap_load_skill), automations, sessions, goals, projects, views, documents (by title). Each object row has an `open` link. An absent block was not searched; `matches: []` = searched, nothing fit; `error` = that read failed. Matching is lexical, so a miss is never proof of absence: read `coverage`, and `noConfidentMatch` for the escalation ladder. Run a hit with synap_run_capability (verbId) or synap_start_session (templateId = playbook id, launch: true).

intent.description: What you want to DO, in your own words (e.g. 'clean up duplicate contacts'). Keep the NOUN — it is the most discriminating word.

workspaceId.description: Optional workspace lens; omit for the whole pod.

catalogs.description: Which catalogs to search. Omit for all. A catalog you leave out is ABSENT from the result, not empty.

tools.name: synap_list_capabilities
tools.description: Discover what the user can actually DO. Returns a SECTIONED view: `integrations` (their connected services + tools, one per name, each with its `verbs` nested — e.g. google → gmail_send, gmail_search, calendar_list; the verb `id` is what you pass to synap_run_capability), `skills` (standalone runnable skills), and `commands`. Each integration shows `connection.connected` (needs connecting if false) and each verb shows `effectiveExecMode` (propose = your run is filed for review, not refused). A verb carrying `blocked: "not_enabled"` is installed but switched off: synap_run_capability WILL refuse it, so do not run it first — hand the user its `enable.url` to turn it on. Core built-in tools (already available to you directly as MCP tools) and teaching docs are folded out of this actionable view BY DEFAULT and only COUNTED under `excluded` — pass kind:"builtin-tool" or kind:"teaching-doc" to list them here instead, or synap_load_skill("catalog") for every teaching doc grouped by topic. Pass `query` to search across integrations/verbs/skills (e.g. query:"send email"). A run refused with DENIED_BY_RULE: the person said never for this agent and this kind of act. It was not done. Do not retry it or do it another way; ask the person if it is needed. Only a pod admin can take that back, in pod admin Settings.

workspaceId.description: Workspace UUID

query.description: Search text (e.g. 'send email', 'calendar'). Ranks + narrows the result instead of returning the full unfiltered dump.

kind.description: Optional exact kind filter: tool | skill | command | source-provider | builtin-tool | teaching-doc.

containerId.description: Only rows belonging to this capability pack (the `containerId` on integrations/skills, or `builtInPack.containerId`). The default view summarises Synap Core's first-party verbs as ONE `builtInPack` line — pass its containerId to list them.

intent.description: Reverse lookup by INTENT slug — what you want to DO, without knowing the vendor. A registry slug (the seed includes search_external, send_message, capture_into_pod, and the rest of the original 13). Returns the concrete verb ids that serve it (pass one to synap_run_capability), each with `enabled` (switched on in the pod) and `runPosture` (auto runs now, propose files a review). Takes precedence over `query`/`kind`/`limit`. An unknown slug is an error from the registry, not an empty list. An empty match list means the slug is known and nothing installed declares it yet — scan without `intent` before concluding the pod cannot do this.

tools.name: synap_list_installations
tools.description: What is installed on the person's computers: one row per capability on a computer (a `tool` such as media-transcribe, or a `service`). Each row: the computer, the capability key, its kind, its `status` (planned, installing, installed, updating, removing, failed), what was asked (`desiredState`, `desiredVersion`, `approvedAt`), what the computer observed (`observedVersion`, `observedOs`, `observedArch`, `verifiedAt`) and `health`, derived at read: ok, degraded (a service reported unhealthy), drifted (not the approved version), stale (a check is due), unknown (not checked yet, or the computer has not reported: offline, not broken) or failed. Filter with `computerId` or `capabilityKey`. `installationId` reads ONE row with its approved snapshot (`manifest`, `digests`), the pod's `current` definition and `drift` (same: an update is a repair; changed: an update asks again). Read-only; to install, update, check or remove, ask with synap_request_installation.

capabilityKey.description: A capability's catalog slug, e.g. media-transcribe: which computers have it.

installationId.description: One installation: its snapshot and drift.

tools.name: synap_request_installation
tools.description: Ask to install a capability on one of the person's computers, or on the pod. Find it with synap_run_capability market.search (kind capability); `computers[].canInstall` says which computer can take it. One call files ONE proposal the person approves on one card: if the pod does not have the capability yet, approving adds it from the marketplace AND installs it on the computer you named (once per capability and computer; a check, or a repair at the approved version, asks nobody). `proposed` is success. A wrong choice answers `status: refused` with a `code`, a `reason` (INSTALLS_FROM_POD_OFF: the person turns on "Installs from the pod" for that computer; UNSUPPORTED_COMPUTER: its system or processor is not supported; RUNS_ON_POD: ask with computer "pod"; RUNS_ON_COMPUTER: name a computer) and `computers` to choose again from. Two computers fit the name: AMBIGUOUS_COMPUTER (`candidates`): ask the person, never pick. After the computer's worker runs it, read the result with synap_list_installations.

tools.name: synap_create_automation
tools.description: Create an automation — a WHEN→THEN flow that reacts to a trigger (event | cron | webhook | manual) by running a flow of steps. Governed the same as every write: an agent create returns status='proposed' for review; on approval it becomes ACTIVE (live) — not a stuck draft. Provide the trigger, a flowDefinition ({ nodes, edges }), and a dataContract — the contract is REQUIRED for agent-authored automations (which this always is) and the create door rejects the automation without a valid one. Cron: triggerConfig.expression (5-field) + timezone (IANA; omitted = UTC). A playbook_run node starts a playbook's session on any trigger. Discover what already exists with synap_list_automations first. Creates it on this pod only; an official template is written in the catalog (synap-app/packages/workspace-templates); landing it on app-bases main publishes it.

E.g. { profileSlug: 'person' }, { profileSlug: { $in: ['person','contact'] } }, { score: { $gt: 30 } }. A bare array value and a nested object value are BOTH rejected: use $in for several values, and a dot-notation key to reach nested data. audience (pod-wide): 'me' (default) or 'everyone'.

tools.name: synap_create_rule
tools.description:
Turn a stated standing intent into a RULE — the COMPILED door, and the one to reach for whenever the user says 'always…', 'from now on…', 'never…', 'every Monday…', or states a preference that should outlive this conversation. Send their own words as `intent`.
• `intent` alone → a FACT rule: durable prose ('Acme prefers async') that any agent reads later while reasoning. Legitimate and complete.
• `intent` + `sentence` → BEHAVIOUR: the door compiles your WHEN/WHERE/THEN into a real automation, or refuses. A rule that describes something running is never stored as prose that cannot run.
USE THIS INSTEAD OF synap_create_automation / synap_create_skill for a standing intent. Those are raw primitives — they persist whatever you hand them, so a bad trigger installs 'active' and silently never fires, and an instruction skill only ever sits there as text. This door verifies the compiled artifact against the runtime BEFORE anything is saved. (Reach for synap_create_automation directly only when you are authoring a flow that is not a user-stated rule — a multi-step pipeline with its own data contract.)
WHAT IT REJECTS, and why each rejection is real: a WHEN naming an event no emitter produces (the automation could never match); a WHERE row with a field but no value (dropping it would widen the rule beyond what was written); a THEN with no configured action (a trigger wired to nothing); `run_command` (the command step has no receiver and throws every run — use an AI step). A refusal comes back as status='denied' with `failure.clause` (WHEN | WHERE | THEN) and a reason written for a human. FIX THAT CLAUSE AND RESEND — it is a verdict, not a transient error, and re-sending it unchanged will fail identically.
If the intent describes something that should run and you send no `sentence`, the receipt carries `needsBehaviour` — the rule was saved as prose and will not execute; say so rather than reporting it as in effect.
Scope: pod-wide by default; pass `workspaceId` for a domain rule, `projectId` for the cross-cutting lens. A `projectId` limit is only enforceable on WHEN events that carry a project — entity.*, entity_facet.*, external_message.*, channel_message.*, focus_session.*, proposal.* — and is REFUSED (status='denied', clause WHEN) on any other trigger (e.g. a schedule); drop the project or pick one of those events. `expiresAt` makes the rule stop applying — pass one whenever the intent is situational ('while we're in the launch push'), because a standing rule with no expiry is one the user must remember to revoke.
Governed like every write: status='proposed' is SUCCESS, not an error — surface the returned link as a markdown link and never report a proposed rule as already in effect.

OMIT actionVerb for ANY activity on that subject — it compiles to the `<subject>.*` wildcard, which is the right choice for the non-entity subjects (notification, proposal, focus_session, external_message …) whose real actions are domain verbs, not create/update/delete. Every subjectCategory offered is producer-backed AND workspace-scoped, so none of them is a trigger that can never fire. triggerType 'cron' → cronFrequency (+ cronTime / cronDays / cronDayOfMonth / cronTimezone). The compiled event pattern is checked against the runtime's own event grammar, so a WHEN nothing emits is refused rather than stored.

Omit it for a prose-only FACT rule. All three keys are required when you send it (`conditions` and `actions` may be empty arrays, but an empty `actions` is refused as 'no THEN').

Omit it and your writes are grouped for you. A grouped session closes after 2 h idle; a closed or foreign id is reported in `attribution.ignoredSession`, never an error.

tools.name: synap_update_rule
tools.description:
Propose a CORRECTION to an existing rule — the governed edit door, the same one the app's rule editor uses. Reach for it when a rule you (or anyone) wrote no longer matches the facts: change its wording, its WHEN/WHERE/THEN, its scope or its review date. Never delete-and-recreate a rule to change it — that loses its id, its run history and its lineage.
FULL SHAPE, not a patch: send the rule as it should be stored. `intent` and `scope` are REQUIRED and replace the stored ones (send the old wording/scope unchanged if you are only fixing the sentence). `expiresAt` and `sentence` have THREE states: omit to KEEP the stored value, `null` to CLEAR it (a `null` sentence makes the rule prose-only and retires its automation), a value to REPLACE it. `draft` defaults to false — editing a draft rule therefore ACTIVATES it, which recompiles the sentence and is refused by clause if it still has a hole; pass `draft: true` to keep it a draft.

If that create came back `proposed`, call synap_get_proposal with its proposalId after a person approved it — the id is `data.materialized.ruleId`. There is no dedicated rule listing on MCP. A workspace rule is only found under its workspace (pass its `workspaceId`); `not_found` means no rule with that id is visible to you.
Refusals are the same as synap_create_rule's: status='denied' with `failure.clause` (WHEN | WHERE | THEN) — fix that clause and resend.
Governed like every write: status='proposed' is SUCCESS, not an error — nothing changes until a person approves it. Surface the returned link as a markdown link and never report a proposed edit as already in effect.

Every subjectCategory offered is producer-backed AND workspace-scoped, so none of them is a trigger that can never fire. triggerType 'cron' → cronFrequency (+ cronTime / cronDays / cronDayOfMonth / cronTimezone). tools.name: synap_create_skill
tools.description: Author a skill: Documentation (always) + OPTIONAL code. Send `body` alone for a TEACHING skill — reusable prose (a process, a checklist, a house style) that any agent later pulls with synap_load_skill; a teaching skill needs a `slug`, because that is the ref load_skill resolves. Send `code` for a runnable sandboxed executable, or both: read synap_load_skill('system/synap/code-skills') first for the runtime (the async (args, context) wrapper, callProvider and its return shape, hubProtocol reads, propose.entity, limits). A code skill that calls an installed tool with callProvider should declare it in `requiredTools`, so a run is approved once, not once more per call. `kind` is derived from code presence — do not guess it. For a deterministic provider HTTP call on an already-installed tool use synap_create_verb instead. Governed like every write: an agent create returns status='proposed'. An agent-authored skill is born UNAPPROVED either way and does NOT load or run until a person approves its proposal — code executes, and instruction prose lands in a future agent's system prompt, so both need a deliberate human OK. That one approval also turns it on: there is no separate enable step (an edit to its code later turns it off until approved again). One name per skill in a scope: a create under a name that already exists here is refused with that skill's id — change it with synap_update_skill instead. Creates it on this pod only; an official template is written in the catalog (synap-app/packages/workspace-templates); landing it on app-bases main publishes it.

instructions:
The user's Synap pod: source of truth. Tool names below are stems; your door may prefix them (`synap_ask`).

1. **Recall first.** `get_*` a known id, else `ask`.
2. **Capture as you go.** A decision, learning, pain (`finding`), win (`proof-point`), fact or task: `capture` it when it happens; about the user: `remember_fact`.
3. **Orient once.** `orient`: pending review, open sessions.
4. **Work in a session.** `start_session` or resume (playbook `templateId`); goal (TRACK): `list_tracks`, else `start_track`; work in it = `start_session` + `trackId`; 2-5 `criteria`; status moves carry `expectedStatus`; person-only: `owner:'human'` slot + `blockedReason` + `ask` (confirm/choose with 1 `recommended`/form/act/provide), then `wait_for_answer` if listed; post progress, questions and results in its room (`post_message` to `session.channelId`); your own chat may repeat them (`Q-<id8>`); chat answer → `relay_answer`, words verbatim; PR = outcome `pr-<repo>-<n>` (`ref.url`); `evaluate_session`, close open asks, `complete_session`.
5. **Never guess a project**: pin only what the user names (`set_*_focus`).
6. **`proposed` is success**: keep going, never retry.
7. **Discover before inventing**: `list_profiles` / `list_capabilities`; **extend**, never a twin.
8. **One space per domain**; projects filter it (`file_into_project`, `project_use_workspace`).

Depth: `load_skill` `system/synap/concepts`, `work-model`, `focus-sessions`, `from-intent`, `escalation-ladder`, `writes`.
